mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown four consecutive weeks of improvement (-61.1 to -58.7). This momentum reflects an ongoing recovery trajectory in consumer foot traffic that is likely to persist, producing a higher mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days than the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose monotonically from -61.1 to -58.7 over the last 4 weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean over the last 28 days despite the four-week uptrend.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week jump in WORKPLACES mobility signals accelerated return-to-office activity, which drives incidental retail visits (lunch, errands, commute-adjacent shopping) and lifts RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises more than 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -54.0 (t-1w) to -50.1 (t-0w), a 3.9 point increase
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the following two weeks despite WORKPLACES exceeding the 3-point weekly increase threshold.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve in the same week, this indicates a coordinated resumption of commuting behavior that compounds to generate larger retail footfall gains than either series alone would predict, raising RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: Both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES increase by more than 2 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -56.3 to -53.9 and WORKPLACES rose from -54.0 to -50.1 in the same week (t-0w)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean despite joint TRANSIT and WORKPLACES co-improvement.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility frees household time previously spent at home, redirecting activity toward discretionary retail and recreation outings, boosting RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below the prior week value
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL dropped from 14.3 (t-2w) to 13.0 (t-1w) before rebounding to 14.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next two weeks following a week-on-week RESIDENTIAL decline.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained multi-week improvement in TRANSIT mobility reflects easing of public transit restrictions or rider confidence, which mechanically enables more retail and recreation visits that depend on public transport access, raising RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -57.3 to -53.9 over four consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next 28 days despite continuous TRANSIT improvement across all four observed weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week rise in GROCERY_PHARM mobility reflects loosening of essential-trip-only behavior, which spills over into general shopping activity and produces a short-term bump in RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises more than 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -28.3 (t-1w) to -24.4 (t-0w), a 3.9 point increase
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the immediately following week after a GROCERY_PHARM jump exceeding 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week surge in PARKS mobility indicates favorable weather or seasonal outdoor demand that substitutes for indoor retail and recreation visits, temporarily suppressing RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 4 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -20.6 (t-2w) to -16.3 (t-1w), a 4.3 point jump, before falling back to -20.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week following a PARKS surge exceeding the 4-point threshold.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain deeply suppressed (below -50) while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated (above +10), this combination signals a persistent stay-at-home regime that structurally caps retail recovery regardless of marginal weekly gains, keeping RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -50 and TRANSIT remains below -50 and RESIDENTIAL remains above +10 simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:All four weeks show WORKPLACES below -50, TRANSIT below -50, and RESIDENTIAL above +13
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining below -50 and RESIDENTIAL remaining above +10 throughout the period.
